identity.description:
Add the plan usage figures and the slow-down of the orchestrator

## Summary

The crew orchestrator can now know the plan usage of the account and slow down before the five-hour limit. Before this change, only one session could see the usage figures, and only as of its own last reply, so a long batch ran from 52% to 92% with no warning. Now every implementer feeds one shared file from its status line, a fresh reading fills the gaps when no session works, and a check tells the orchestrator and each implementer when to slow down, stop, and start again after the reset. The user's own status line stays in each tab.

Closes #153

**Ticket:** [#153 — plan usage figures and the automatic slow-down](https://github.com/jerridan/crew/issues/153), part 3 of [#150](https://github.com/jerridan/crew/issues/150)
**Type:** New feature

---

## Agent context

### Authority

- `skills/orchestrator/references/usage.md` (new) owns the shared file, the merge rule, which sessions contribute, the levels and their exit codes, the launch value, the watch, the slow-down rule and the limit.
- `skills/project-lead/references/autonomy-contract.md`, "The usage limit line", owns what a project lead does with a `Usage limit:` charter line.
- `skills/project-lead/references/record-format.md` lists the charter line. `skills/project-lead/SKILL.md` writes it into the charter and lists the `Usage limit` standing-instructions section.
- The orchestrator record and its `pace` object (mode, slots, limit) belong to issue 151 (`skills/orchestrator/references/orchestrator-record.md`, `crew-orch.py pace set`). This PR defines no copy of them.
- `docs/design.md` §15.NNN records the probe and the design. The orchestrator assigns the number.

### Where the orchestrator and an implementer read the figures and the limit

- Figures: both run `python3 <plugin>/skills/orchestrator/scripts/crew-usage.py check --limit <pct>` (level, exit 0/10/20) or `show --json` (figures). The board runs `show --json`. The file is `<record-root>/usage.json`.
- Limit: the orchestrator reads `pace.limit_pct` from its own record (issue 151). An implementer reads the `Usage limit: <pct>` line of its charter, which only the orchestrator writes into the goal it sends, as a copy of `pace.limit_pct`; the orchestrator resends it when the limit changes.
- Wake: the orchestrator arms `crew-usage.py watch --limit <pct>` with `Monitor`; it prints a line only when the level changes or the window resets. An implementer stopped at the limit arms `crew-usage.py wait` in the background and resumes when it exits.

### What changed, by file

- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/crew-usage.py` (new): `record`, `statusline` (records the sample, then runs the user's own status line with the same stdin), `settings` (prints the `--settings` value for the launcher), `refresh` (a fresh reading from `claude --restricted --strict-mcp-config` with no prompt and no model turn), `show`, `check`, `watch`, `wait`.
- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-crew-usage.py` (new): 70 seeded checks with a stub `claude`, a temp HOME and a temp record root.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/usage.md` (new): the reference above.
- `skills/project-lead/references/autonomy-contract.md`: new section "The usage limit line".
- `skills/project-lead/references/record-format.md`: the `Usage limit: <pct>` charter line.
- `skills/project-lead/SKILL.md`: the charter line at "Take the goal"; the `Usage limit` row in the standing-instructions table, with the count changed to twelve.
- `CLAUDE.md`: the layout rows, the code-exceptions sentence, the build state and the authority list.
- `docs/design.md`: the §15.NNN entry.
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`: the placeholder version `0.1.NNN-issue-153`. The orchestrator assigns the number.

### Constraints that applied

- No probe or test changed a settings file, and no `claude` start loaded the user's plugins: the only real start is `claude --restricted --strict-mcp-config --settings <json>`, which reads no settings file. The tests check settings-file modification times.
- Python 3 standard library only. No dollar budget.
- One rule in one file: the project-lead side points at `usage.md`, and the record's `pace` object stays issue 151's.
- The plugin version and the §15 number are placeholders, as the orchestrator asked.
- The README does not change: the only user-facing item is the `Usage limit` standing-instructions section, which only the orchestrator reads, and the orchestrator skill (issue 154) is not built yet. Its README row belongs with issue 154.

### How this was verified

- `python3 skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-crew-usage.py` prints `70 of 70 checks passed`. A seeded fault (the same-window merge reversed) gave `65 of 68` before the last fix round, then passed again after the revert.
- Probe of the source, before the spec: a status line in a `claude --restricted` start got `rate_limits` 5 seconds after the start with no prompt (10%). It stayed at 10% for 4.5 idle minutes, and moved to 14% after one one-word prompt. A mod's `$.session.usage()` read 1% for the same window at the same time.
- Live run of `refresh` once: five-hour 31%, seven-day 35%, in 7.5 seconds, no process left.
- Live tab check of the wrapper: a `claude --restricted --settings "$(crew-usage.py settings)"` tab showed the user's own four-line status line, and the shared file got the sample within 12 seconds.

### Known gaps

- No orchestrator run has used any of this yet. The orchestrator skill (issue 154) and the board pane (issue 155) are the readers.
- Not tested: whether an in-process subagent's or teammate's API reply refreshes the figures of its parent session's status line.
- A fresh reading must run in a directory that `claude` already trusts. In another directory it fails after 30 seconds and `check` falls back to the stored file.
- The 15-point margin assumes a burn of at most 2 points a minute, as experiment 1 measured. A faster burn can pass the limit between readings.

findings.claim: A repeated sample with the same window and percent counts as newer, so an idle session's periodic status line refresh keeps moving updated_at and the file never looks stale.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a strict > for the same-window case, so only a higher percent or a later window moves updated_at.
findings.explanation: Idle implementers repeat their old figure every refresh, which resets updated_at, suppresses the fresh reading, and flattens the forecast rate.

findings.claim: If the refresh times out after the status line ran but before figures arrived, the account is wrongly marked plan_limits false.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark plan_limits false only when claude exited or stayed up for a set time without figures, not when the time limit cut it short.
findings.explanation: A slow start is treated like an account with no plan limits, and check reports normal for up to 5 minutes.

finding.explanation: A slow start is treated like an account with no plan limits, and check reports normal for up to 5 minutes.
